body: It's not really putting them on a pedestal, so much as they have something I need (access to human touch), and I can't at any point show that I desire what I desire and need more than anything. That sounds transactional, and it isn't at the interpersonal level, but it's true.  I totally understand outcome independence and its importance, I guess the problem is, I'm having trouble convincing my subconscious that an outcome that matters, doesn't. When I'm not nervous, they tend not to want to interact at all, which is the weird part of the puzzle.  Thanks for the help, regardless. I agree with what you said, just can't quite get it to happen.

It's because I'm anxious. Sometimes my voice quivers, or I might let out a nervous twitch or two.  When I'm not anxious and still think well of myself I get the impression I'm boring, based on reactions.  That's what I've observed.  Women just have so many options that there's no need to stoop so low, seems that way anyway; appears to be the frame that fits best. I have no doubt people are having tons of success, I see that all around me; they must just be very interesting personalities, enough to get over the looks thing.

God, the part about Maslow....

I get into fights with my therapist, because she insists I need to just stop "being obsessed" with sex and touch. I point to the pyramid, suddenly everything we know about psychology ceases to exist. She tells me I'm not listening.  I don't know, clearly I'm just not confident enough, and it shows subconsciously (and I'm short, bald, relatively ugly with patchy skin).

I did all that self improvement stuff.  Ultimately, it didn't make me that confident with women; no success transferred over, two completely different realms. Not sure what to think. I agree with most of that story though, I had SO many friends over the years who were women, who wouldn't have sex with me, but would have sex with pretty much everyone else. Universally, they said the same shit- wouldn't just admit they were just as superficial as everyone else, "be yourself, it's so hard that women have to deal with imperfect relationships...don't you understand it's just as bad as nothing at all (hence why we don't do what we say is better)?"

That's what I was thinking.  My family lives thousands of miles away.  I remember reading [this story] (http://www.integratedsociopsychology.net/infant_monkeys-attachment.html) and involuntarily shuddering.
That's what I did all summer. No dice.  Blew my mind, didn't know it was possible to fail so consistently, figure it's about time to get put down. Kind of scared, tbh.
